# Understanding Reactivity

Your group's task is to improve a Shiny app through the use of *reactive expressions*. To do this, you will identify flaws in the above version of the Shiny app and edit the code to implement solutions.

This activity will guide your through the adaptation of this Shiny app.

## Part 1: on your own

Start with [`bootstrap-start/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/apps/bootstrap-start/app.R): click **Copy raw file**, then paste it into a new `app.R` file in RStudio.

1.  To begin, you need to understand what the Shiny app is doing. Run the Shiny app. What output changes when you change...

  a.  the number of bootstrap resamples?

  b.  the number of histogram bins?

  c.  the confidence level?

2.  Looking back at #1, are there any surprises? Does anything change/update unexpectedly? Does anything fail to update?

## Part 2: with those around you (I recommend groups of 3)

3.  Discuss your answers to Part 1 with your group and be ready to report back.

4.  Read through the code in the `renderPlot()` and `renderTable()` expressions. Note the key tasks executed within each.

5.  Based on your answers to #4, Is there any replication? That is, are any key tasks executed multiple times? Record your group's answers and be ready to report back.

::: callout-warning
## Stop here

Stop here and let Amanda know that you've finished. We'll regroup and discuss reactivity shortly
:::

## Part 3

6.  Create a list of reactive values/expressions that should be created outside the `render*` statements. Recall that reactive values are the inputs/objects that observers watch for updates.

7.  For each reactive expression you identify in step #6, identify which output (the histogram or the confidence interval) should *observe* that expression and update when it is changed?

8.  Use your answers to steps #6-7 to reorganize the server-side code for this Shiny app. (You don't need to change the inputs!) To do this, first create any reactive expressions. Next, adapt the `renderPlot()` and `renderTable()` chunks to use your reactive expressions. Remember to run your app regularly to help pinpoint bugs.

9.  Compare and contrast the performance and readability of the revised app's code to the original "non-modularized" version.

# `manager-survey` app

Return to the app from Friday: your own version, or paste in [`v2-filter/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/apps/v2-filter/app.R) (**Copy raw file**, then paste over your `app.R`).

10. The `filter(industry %in% input$industry)` code is written twice. Create a reactive expression called `filtered()` and use it in both plots.
11. Add `req(input$industry)` as the first line of `filtered()`. Uncheck every industry. What changed?
12. Add a `textOutput("n_respondents")` that says "Showing 7,003 respondents", using `filtered()`. (Hint: `paste("Showing", scales::comma(nrow(filtered())), "respondents")`.)
13. Add a table of the filtered data: `DT::dataTableOutput("data")` in the UI and `DT::renderDataTable({ filtered() })` in the server.

The finished version is [`v3-reactive/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/apps/v3-reactive/app.R).

# UI design

## Reorganize the manager survey app

Start from your `v3` app, or [`v3-reactive/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/apps/v3-reactive/app.R). 

14. Move the inputs into a `sidebarPanel()` and the outputs into a `mainPanel()`, inside `sidebarLayout()`.
15. Put each plot, and the data table, on its own tab (`tabsetPanel()` and `tabPanel()`).
16. Give every input a plain-language label (not `xcol`!), and add axis labels and titles to the plots.
17. Add a fourth tab with a line plot of the *average* salary by `education`, with one line for each selected industry.

::: callout-tip
## Hint

`group_by(industry, education) |> summarize(mean_salary = mean(annual_salary))`, then `geom_line()` with `group = industry`. Don't forget to use `filtered()`!
:::

18. (If time) 25 checkboxes make the sidebar very long. Can you replace them with a `selectInput(..., multiple = TRUE)`?
